Postdoc in Neural Circuits of Sensorimotor Control We are seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher for a project investigating the neural circuit mechanisms underlying sensorimotor control and adaptive behavior. The research will take place at the Department of Neuroscience, University of Copenhagen, in the Bellardita Laboratory , as part of a research program supported by a Lundbeck Foundation Ascending Investigator Grant . You will join an international and interdisciplinary research environment combining systems neuroscience, quantitative behavior and computational approaches to understand how neural circuits generate and adapt movement. Our research The Bellardita Laboratory studies how neural circuits generate, monitor and adapt movement. Our work focuses on understanding how neural activity across the nervous system is transformed into coordinated behavior and how sensory information contributes to the control and modification of movement. We combine experimental systems neuroscience with advanced behavioral analysis and computational approaches. Our experimental approaches include in vivo neural recording and imaging, optogenetic and genetic manipulation of neural circuits, quantitative analysis of movement and behavior, and computational analysis of large neural and behavioral datasets . A major goal of the laboratory is to understand the principles through which neural circuits integrate internal motor signals and sensory information to support flexible behavior. We investigate these questions across different forms of movement and levels of the nervous system. The laboratory is part of the Department of Neuroscience at the University of Copenhagen and is embedded within a strong research environment in neural circuits, motor control, sensory systems and systems neuroscience. We collaborate with research groups in Denmark and internationally and aim to provide a supportive environment in which postdoctoral researchers can develop both technically and scientifically. More information about our research can be found at: https://in.ku.dk/research/bellardita-lab/ Position Responsibilities The postdoctoral researcher will investigate neural circuit mechanisms involved in the control and adaptation of movement. Responsibilities Will Include Designing and conducting experiments in behaving mice. Recording and manipulating neural activity using advanced systems neuroscience approaches. Developing and applying quantitative behavioral paradigms. Analysing neural and behavioral data using computational and statistical approaches. Contributing to the development of new experimental approaches within the project. Preparing scientific publications and presenting results at national and international meetings. The postdoctoral researcher will play a central role in the project and will have opportunities to develop independent scientific questions within its broader research framework. Candidate profile We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic scientist with a strong interest in neural circuits and behavior. Essential Experience And Skills PhD in Neuroscience, Neurobiology, Physiology, Biomedical Engineering or a related discipline. Experimental experience in systems, circuit or behavioral neuroscience. Experience working with rodents. Experience with at least one method for recording and manipulating neural activity in vivo. In vivo calcium imaging, in vivo Electrophysiology, Optogenetic or chemogenetic manipulation, Viral-vector and stereotaxic approaches. Experience with quantitative analysis of experimental data using Python, MATLAB or comparable tools. Ability to design, perform and troubleshoot experiments independently. Proficient communication skills and ability to work collaboratively within a research team. Excellent English skills, both written and spoken. Desirable Experience And Skills Experience in one or more of the following areas would be an advantage: Quantitative behavioral analysis. Motor or sensorimotor neuroscience. Computational analysis of neural population activity. Machine-learning approaches for neural or behavioral data. Development of behavioral tasks in rodents. Applicants are not expected to have experience with all of these methods . We particularly welcome researchers with strong expertise in one relevant experimental area who are interested in expanding their methodological repertoire. Place of employment You will be employed at the Department of Neuroscience, University of Copenhagen , at the Panum Institute in central Copenhagen. The successful applicant will join a dynamic and international neuroscience environment. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions, access to modern experimental facilities, and opportunities to interact with researchers across systems neuroscience, neural circuits, motor control, computational neuroscience and biomedical engineering. The postdoctoral researcher will be a major participant in the scientific development of the project, from experimental design and data collection to analysis, interpretation, publication and presentation of the work at international conferences. review_candidates.description: The IQVIA sponsor-dedicated Clinical Functional Service Partnerships (Clinical FSP) department is supporting our client’s project team in the execution of clinical trials. Has the overall responsibility for the study commitments within the country and for timely delivery of data to required quality. Provides Project Oversight & Leadership for Clinical Deliverables Leads and manages the clinical teams Leads and supports the relevant staff (ie. local start-up staff, local and global regulatory affairs staff, inhouse clinical staff, etc) to drive successful activation of trial sites Monitors the quality of clinical activities and addresses quality issues with the appropriate team member Reviews and approves site visit reports within agreed turnaround times and ensures tracking, follow up, and resolution of site issues Works with the relevant staff to identify data related issues and risks to clinical activities; develops contingency and mitigation plans to minimize risks Creates and maintains project-specific plans, documents, and tools for the clinical team Supports the CRAs with site monitoring activities and provides suggestions and solutions to site issues Oversees the relevant regulatory and in-house clinical staff to ensure that all non-safety periodic updates, progress reports, and renewals, and/or end of study notifications are performed in accordance with the trial protocol, local regulations, ICH GCP, and any other processes or procedures governing the clinical trial Acts as coordinating manager to ensure consistency of training, processes, and systems-related activities as well as ad-hoc coordinating activities Required Skills And Qualifications Bachelor degree in related discipline, preferably in life science Five or more years of experience in clinical research, including a minimum of 2 years' project management experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience sufficient to successfully perform the key responsibilities of the job Good knowledge of international guidelines ICH GCP as well as relevant local regulations Proven ability to lead and motivate cross functional teams to deliver clinical trials according to or ahead of time plan, budget and with required quality Previous work experience in TA's: Oncology or Onco-hematology is required Good knowledge of the Drug Development Process Excellent knowledge of spoken and written English language. We appreciate your honesty and professionalism.
